measured: `(( expr ))` used as a COMMAND does not abort the enclosing top-level command on either bash: `{ (( kt_r + 1 )); echo x; }` with kt_r=kt_r, and `{ (( 1 + )); echo x; }`, print the diagnostic and then run `echo x` (the (( returns 1). Arithmetic EXPANSION `$(( ))` and an assoc/indexed subscript error (empty key, [-1] on an empty array) abort the whole { } block. The fixtures therefore use $(( )). A stray `(( bad ))` in a test is still caught by the diagnostic grep.

A bash fatal diagnostic is prefixed with the file the failing CODE lives in: an error inside a library function called from a test prints `<lib.sh>: line N:`, not the test file. KT_BASH_FATAL_DIAG_RE therefore accepts any file prefix (first char alnum or / . _ ~ -, optional drive letter; a line starting with `[` or an ANSI escape cannot match).
5.3.9 prints `arithmetic syntax error` where 5.2.37 prints `syntax error`; the regex term `syntax error` covers both.
`source FILE` returns the status of FILE's last command: a file ending in `[[ -n "" ]] && echo x` gives src_rc 1 on both bashes - the same value a file-scope `return 1` gives (see D1).
Child rc: set -u on an unset variable and ${v:?} -> 127; exit 3 -> 3; set -e; false -> 1 (5.2.37).

Scan cost unchanged: on a 20000-line capture the old kt_runner_find_last_counts_line takes 8.94 s and the new single-pass kt_runner_scan_capture 9.04 s (both bound by `read` from a process substitution, ~0.45 ms/line).
deviations: D1 (plan conflict): section 2.2 says END with src_rc != 0 -> FAILED; section 3 says a last-command-rc-1 file must stay green. Both cannot hold: such a file has src_rc 1, the same value as `return 1`. Implemented: src_rc >= 2 -> `source returned rc=N`; rc 1 alone is no verdict. A file-scope `return N` inside a test block is still caught by the unclosed-test detector for every N (034 a_return asserts both causes for N=4); what goes undetected is only a `return 1` BETWEEN tests. Rejected alternative: a RETURN trap comparing $? at the end of the source with the source rc (tells most `return N` from falling off the end) - it adds a trap to the test shell, and thttpserver 001/003/006/008 run `set -T` DEBUG-trap canaries under which an inherited RETURN trap would fire on every function return.
D2: the diagnostic grep matches a diagnostic from ANY file (the plan writes `^<file>:`), because class-B aborts inside library code carry the library path (measured above).

D3: the signature regex lives in a new dependency-free file ktest_env_signatures.sh (KT_ENV_FORK_FAILURE_RE): timing_check.sh is a standalone tool that cannot source ktest_runner.sh (which needs ktest_core.sh).

D4: the `[FAIL] <file>: source aborted (...)` line is plain text (no ANSI colour): the threaded path runs kt_runner_execute_single_test in an xargs bash where the readonly KT_RED constants do not exist.

D5: several causes are joined with `; ` (e.g. `source returned rc=2; test aborted mid-block; bash error at f.sh:6: syntax error near unexpected token`); the fold is applied once (+1/+1) whatever the number of causes.

D6: test 022's two nested directory-scan fixtures (kt_test_start + kt_assert_equals, never closed) are now judged aborted inside 022; 022 asserts only TESTS_TOTAL >= 2 and discards their output, so it stays green (the plan predicted this).
